newsitem.title: UK: Shield says partner talks to last to yr end.
newsitem.headline: Shield says partner talks to last to yr end.

text.p: Britain's Shield Diagnostics Group Plc said on Tuesday that talks with potential development and marketing partners for its heart attack prediction test were unlikely to come to a conclusion before the end of 1997.

Managing director Gordon Hall also told a news conference following full-year results that he expected U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) approval of Shield's test for blood-clotting agent Activated Factor Twelve (AFT) to take between four and six months.
Weekend press reports suggested the FDA would take only three months to complete its deliberations.
Hall said talks on finding a partner were "ongoing and have been for some time. These discussions remain positive. We'll get an idea of the conclusions by the end of this calendar year."

Shield wants a major partner or partners to develop versions of the test for AFT to enable it achieve maximum sales. It believes AFT is a far more accurate predictor of propensity to heart attacks and heart disease than cholesterol levels.

Although it has not disclosed which companies are involved in discussions, major diagnostic companies such as Abbott Laboratories, Johnson & Johnson, Bayer AG and Boehringer Mannheim are thought to be the most likely candidates.
Shield already has an exploratory diagnostic test research agreement with Abbott.

Earlier this month the Scottish company submitted its own version of the AFT test to U.S. regulators for approval. Hall said this would allow the company to sell the product commercially. Currently it is only available in the U.S. for research use.
Commenting on weekend press reports that approval could take three months, Hall said, "My own judgement is that it is likely to be between four and six months for approval."
Regulatory approval is not required for marketing the test in Europe.
